title: I connected an AI agent to Tiled: it created the tilesets, Wang terrains, layers, and the complete map (opensource project)
author: Samariuml
selftext:
I’ve been working on tiled-ai, an open-source bridge between AI agents and Tiled Map Editor.

It combines a TypeScript MCP server with a Tiled extension, allowing an agent to inspect the current map, understand selections and layers, examine tileset images, create TSX tilesets and Wang terrain sets, and modify the map directly with Undo support.

For this demo, I only specified the visual direction: LPC-style assets. Codex using GPT-6 Astra searched for suitable images, analyzed their tile grids, generated the TSX and TMX files, configured the Wang terrains, and assembled the map across several layers.

The map composition shown here was created entirely by the AI workflow. The source pixel art itself was created by human artists and is properly credited in the repository. A second prompt was needed to refine the house, and the video is sped up.

One lesson from the experiment is that image discovery and technical tileset generation already work surprisingly well, while visually complex structures still benefit from iterative direction.

Project and source code: [https://github.com/rpgjs/tiled-ai](https://github.com/rpgjs/tiled-ai)

I’d be interested to know: would you use this inside an existing Tiled workflow? Which operations should an AI map editor support next? How much autonomy would you give it before requiring a preview?

comments.author: kantorcodes1
comments.body: when Codex uses `apply_operations`, does the whole batch land as one Tiled undo step even if it mixes tile edits, layer changes, and object edits? that boundary seems pretty important once you let it make larger edits without previewing every move.

replies.author: Samariuml
replies.body: Yes. `apply_operations` groups tile, existing-layer, and object edits for one document into a single Tiled Undo step. External tilesets use their own Undo history. The batch is prevalidated, and any partial failure is reported explicitly.

comments.author: Anxious-Cress701
comments.body: Nice work. I found that Wang tiles need the corner bitmask in 3x3 form for Tiled to apply terrain properly, so make sure your agent outputs 48 tile IDs per set.

replies.author: Samariuml
replies.body: Thanks! Tiled uses eight Wang values per tile to describe the four edges and four corners. Some tilesets use a 48-tile layout, but Tiled doesn’t require exactly 48 tiles. tiled-ai supports both known layouts and individually analyzed tilesets.
